After the wet dark days, the country seems more populous. It peoples itself in the sunbeams. The garden, mimic of spring, is gay with flowers.' Sentences three to five, exactly as quoted, commas included. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match; Dorothy Wordsworth at 2 of 3 (months 4 and 10), so a third line in December is allowed and she is not repeated in the month. Not banned; Diary is the right tag; in scope; publishable; source leads with the name, no dash, 114 characters. Weak points, none fatal: (1) fame rests on 'the opening entry' rather than the opening line (the opening line is 'The green paths down the hill-sides are channels for streams'), so rule 2 is met only in the looser sense of the opening passage; (2) 'The Alfoxden Journal' is the conventional modern title; Knight prints an editorial heading, 'Dorothy Wordsworth's Journal, Written at Alfoxden', and footnotes that the MS has no title; (3) the Alfoxden manuscript has been lost since Knight used it, so his text is the only witness and cannot be checked against the MS; a one-line note saying so would be honest. Knight is otherwise known for silent cuts, but these three sentences are also the standard text in later editions (Moorman, Oxford), which depend on him.
